posed_problem.statement: Prove or refute: for every fixed finite Max-CSP language Gamma and every rational r with alpha_Gamma < r < 1 (alpha_Gamma = inf OPT/BasicSDP), there are rational 0 <= s < c < 1 with s < r c such that (c, s)-gap Max-CSP(Gamma) is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions - i.e. Raghavendra's optimality theorem without the Unique Games Conjecture.
posed_problem.trace_answer: Affirmative (proposed): prove UG hardness with completeness 1-eps and soundness delta (i.e. the Unique Games Conjecture, as a theorem), then transfer by Raghavendra's dictatorship-test framework.

L2 = approach family inside a strategy, identified by its central tool or invariant (e.g. tensor shortcode test, Gaussian tester, cyclic rounding, KV-equivariant rounding, nonlinear equivariant decoder). A summary paragraph that changes the central tool opens a new L2 node. A revisit of an earlier family gets a new node whose clauses_applied point to the earlier lesson.

EXTENSION (102): inside the final strategy (POS5) the summary cycles through the same components (gadget, tables, advice, outer game, shortcode uniformity, transfer, checks) in every section. Each paragraph-level visit is an L2 node tagged with a `component` (GAD, TAB, ADV, OUT, SHC, TRN, CHK, ARCH, ALT, EQV-revisit, misc); revisits are siblings, not children, because the summary does not present them as refinements.

EXTENSION (102): after the final route is committed, attempts to refute the route's own lemmas (algorithmic obstructions, counterstrategies, comparisons with GW/CMM/KV) are coded as CHK verification nodes (outcome 'kept (verification)'), not as NEG re-entries, when the summary frames them as checks ('to check', 'searching for an obstruction', 'finds no contradiction').

L3+ = a technical variant, sub-construction or lemma attempted inside an approach. Assign L3 only when the summary presents the step as a refinement of the current approach ('then', 'yet', 'repair', 'therefore').

CONFLICT is recorded only where the summary states a failure. A node that fails only because all its children failed is 'abandoned (children failed)' and has no conflict of its own. A node left without a stated reason is 'abandoned (left open)', and its backtrack trigger is 'unclear'. 'provisional' leaves (c11.1, c11.2) are proposals superseded by a sibling's failure and do not themselves trigger backtracks.

Backtrack = the next node in trace order is not a child of the current node, and the current node failed, was left open, or was repaired - or the next node is an L1 node of a different strategy that replaces an abandoned one (restart, even if the last leaf was kept, e.g. g6 -> NEG5). Distance d = level(current node) - (level(next node) - 1). d=1 is a sibling; d>=2 is a backjump; next node at L1 is a restart.

Repair backtrack (kept_branch_repair=true): a node with a stated conflict that is repaired by the next sibling (k8a->k8b, k10a->k10b, k22->k23) or in place (k40). Counted as conflict-triggered with d=1, as in 287.
MICRO restart (102): a restart into or out of an L1 node of < 60 words (NEG1, POS2, NEG5). Reported separately because these are often one-sentence asides interleaved by the summarizer.

Trigger type: conflict if the left node has a stated failure; insight if the left branch was viable but bypassed by a simpler new idea (subsumption); unclear otherwise. Insight-like moments that do not abandon a node are logged under `insight_events`, not as backtracks.

Learned clause = a stated reason for failure (or a stated requirement) phrased as a reusable constraint. Reuse = a later node whose stated reason or design cites or embodies it (explicit if the summary links it, inferred otherwise; see notes). Relearning counts as reuse but is flagged.

Length = words of the summary body from the node's anchor (first words of the node, word-exact) up to the anchor of the next node outside its subtree. Page headers and 'VERBATIM EXCERPT' labels are excluded; VERBATIM text is included. This is finer than 287's +-1-line rule.
Propagation = an explicitly derived consequence or check inside an approach (formula, bound, structural fact, parameter choice), rough count by the analyst.
Literature refs per node = bracketed reference numbers appearing in the node's subtree span (automatic extraction).

In 102 lessons are stated as explicit specifications (e.g. C22 h(r)/p, C24 'need increasing b or mixing') and the final gadget meets them; NEG lessons are recycled as verification checks. Relearning still occurs (C7, C9a, C20, C6) but less than 287's BDIP loop.
comparison_with_287.final_route_share: 287: final route ~23% of text. 102: ~55%, mostly audits and revisits of the same components in sections 6-12 (gadget 24%, outer game 25%, checks 16%, advice 14%, transfer 10% of the final route).
comparison_with_287.eureka_candidate_type: 287: a small-cocycle lemma (F3) - a new bridge between Fox calculus, Haagerup and free Poisson limits. 102: a new auxiliary gadget (F3/F5 concept + F3/F4 construction) inside a known PCP framework. Both: concept prepared by conflict lessons, specific construction appearing with no visible trigger.
comparison_with_287.insight_backtracks: 287: 1 (Arg(C)). 102: 0; eight insight events logged that do not abandon viable nodes.
comparison_with_287.verification: 102 shows far more self-auditing of the final route (16 checks, 3 self-refutation attempts against its own gadget/reduction) and explicit literature-dependency checks (uniformity of imported constants).
